title: Distillation math: teacher, student, consistency
hook: How a slow sampler's work becomes one model call, on a problem with an exact answer. What a student can copy, what it can't, and what core runs.

verified.claim: The lab's exact path is the probability-flow ODE for Gaussian data, with the Euler step in the form of comfy/k_diffusion/sampling.py.

Core has an LCM sampling type, an lcm sampler and SDTurboScheduler. A search of comfy_extras and core Python finds no node that trains by distillation: TrainLoraNode's loss compares with the clean latent.

Progressive distillation halves the steps each round, and consistency models map noise to data directly, allow multistep sampling, and can be trained by distilling or alone: from the papers' abstracts.
LCM's abstract says it's inspired by consistency models, directly predicts the ODE solution in latent space, and reports 2 to 4 steps at 768 x 768.

unchecked: We read the three papers' abstracts only. The student and consistency fits in the lab are our simplified version: no network, no EMA, one number per level.

On this problem every sampler step is a multiplication, so a student copies its teacher perfectly. A real network does not, so the lab's flat student-error column overstates what a real student keeps.
We ran no distilled model here. The settings in d_lcm are the usual ones for LCM files, and are untested by us. Check your file's notes.
